keyVerseText: And the sons of Japhlet; Pasach, and Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the children of Japhlet.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun פָּסַךְ (Pâçak) derives from an unused root meaning "to divide" or "to cut off," suggesting the idea of separation or distinction. This etymological insight highlights a literal sense of being a "divider" or one who is set apart, which goes beyond the common English transliteration as simply a proper name. Understanding this root meaning enriches the perception of the name as not just an identifier but as one carrying the nuance of separation or distinction within a community or lineage.
usageInScripture: The word פָּסַךְ appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 7:33, where it is used as a proper name, Pasach, an Israelite from the tribe of Asher. It is consistently translated as "Pasach," reflecting its function as a personal name rather than a common noun. This singular occurrence emphasizes its role in genealogical records, underscoring the importance of lineage and tribal identity in the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Though פָּסַךְ appears only as a personal name, its root meaning of "to divide" or "to cut off" invites reflection on the biblical theme of God's people being set apart. The concept of division or distinction resonates with the calling of Israel as a holy nation, separated for God's purposes. In Christ, believers are called out from the world, made distinct as God's own. Thus, even a name like Pasach reminds us of the spiritual reality of separation from sin and the world, and the calling to live in holiness and faithfulness within God's covenant community.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 7:33, the verse lists Pasach as one of the sons of Japhlet, highlighting his place within the tribe of Asher. The use of פָּסַךְ here identifies a distinct individual within the genealogy, emphasizing the importance of family lines in God's unfolding plan. The name's root meaning of "divider" subtly underscores the role of each person in the community as part of God's distinct people, called to be separate and set apart for His purposes.
